story: According to Iroquois legend, at the time of creation the sky goddess Atahensic, also called Sky Woman, lived in the Upper World. While digging up a tree she left a hole in the ground that opened onto a great sky beneath which lay water, and she fell through it. Birds caught her and carried her down onto the water, where a giant turtle rose from the depths for her to rest upon. There she gave birth to twin sons, Hahgwehdiyu (the good twin, called Sapling) and Hahgwehdaetgah (the evil twin, called Flint). Hahgwehdiyu was born normally, but Hahgwehdaetgah burst from her side, killing her. From her death, Hahgwehdiyu created the sky and, from her head, the sun; Hahgwehdaetgah then made darkness to drive the sun away. Hahgwehdiyu made the moon and stars from her breasts and set them, as his sisters, to guard the night. He gave the rest of her body to the earth, calling her the Great Mother, and planted a seed in her corpse from which corn grew as a gift to mankind. In another version, Atahensic is instead the grandmother of the twins; her daughter Tekawerahkwa was impregnated by the west wind and died giving birth to them. Wishing her body to sustain the people, or through seeds Atahensic sowed on her grave, Tekawerahkwa's remains grew into corn, beans, and squash from her breasts, hands, and navel; sunflowers from her legs; strawberries from her heart; tobacco from her head; and purple potatoes from her feet.
blind: According to a people's legend, at the time of creation a sky goddess lived in the world above. While digging up a tree she left a hole in the ground that opened onto a great sky beneath which lay water, and she fell through it. Birds caught her and carried her down onto the water, where a giant turtle rose from the depths for her to rest upon. There she gave birth to twin sons, a good twin and an evil twin. The good twin was born normally, but the evil twin burst from her side, killing her. From her death, the good twin created the sky and, from her head, the sun; the evil twin then made darkness to drive the sun away. The good twin made the moon and stars from her breasts and set them, as his sisters, to guard the night. He gave the rest of her body to the earth, calling her the Great Mother, and planted a seed in her corpse from which a grain crop grew as a gift to mankind. In another version, the sky goddess is instead the grandmother of the twins; her daughter was impregnated by the west wind and died giving birth to them. Wishing her body to sustain the people, or through seeds the sky goddess sowed on her grave, the daughter's remains grew into a grain crop, a bean crop, and a squash-like vegetable from her breasts, hands, and navel; a flowering plant from her legs; a berry plant from her heart; a smoking herb from her head; and a root vegetable from her feet.
title: Atahensic
